item.title: Nationalist Party proposes Judge Lawrence Mintoff for chief justice
item.description: The PN has proposed Judge Lawrence Mintoff for the post of chief justice just 24 hours after the government proposed Judge Miriam Hayman • Appointment of chief justice requires two-thirds parliamentary majority

item.title: Man granted bail after admitting to downloading child sex abuse material
item.description: Court orders pre-sentencing report as 31-year-old, who pleaded guilty to possessing material involving children under nine, placed under supervision

item.title: Paschalino Cefai charged with assaulting partner, breaching bail conditions
item.description: A 46-year-old repeat offender from Żebbuġ, Gozo remanded in custody after alleged domestic incident in Birkirkara

item.title: Man arrested in Marsa over suspected cannabis trafficking
item.description: Police say suspect found with 30 packets of cannabis as force reiterates zero-tolerance approach to illegal sales

item.title: Protesters call on Malta to withdraw from Eurovision over Israel’s participation
item.description: Artists and activists urge government to suspend involvement in the Eurovision Song Contest, saying art cannot be separated from politics

item.title: Alex Borg defends bishop on childcare comments
item.description: Opposition Leader Alex Borg says Gozo Bishop Anton Teuma was unfairly attacked for remarks on childcare centres, stressing the issue lies with systemic family measures rather than parents

item.title: From chief justice row to cannabis reform: Alex Borg makes his case for government
item.description: In a candid session at the MaltaToday newsroom, the Opposition leader set out his positions on justice, planning, transport and party financing

item.title: Alex Borg’s biggest challenge now
item.description: The obvious problems the PN has been talking about do concern people but on their own may not necessarily determine how they will ultimately vote in an election

item.title: WATCH | Wayne Flask: ‘Planning bills are rotten to the core’
item.description: Wayne Flask is secretary of Il-Kollettiv, a residents’ activist group, and a member of the consultation board set up to find middle ground on government’s controversial planning reforms. He tells Matthew Farrugia that government is intentionally dragging its feet on the issue to quietly move the bills away from public eyes on the eve of the next general election.
